changes.before: Implement TimedTask extending the supplied Task. Initialize title through super, store minutes, and override describe to return the parent description followed by " / N min". Inputs meet the stated string/number contract.
changes.after: Build a more specific class using a class that already exists.

before: extends establishes an inheritance relationship. TimedTask instances can use Task behavior and add their own minutes. A derived constructor must call super(...) before accessing this; that call initializes the instance through the parent constructor.

TimedTask.describe overrides the inherited method. super.describe() calls the parent implementation with the same instance as its receiver. It returns the title text; the override adds duration text. Calling this.describe() from this override instead would recurse into itself, not select the parent method.
Keep Task unchanged and implement TimedTask. Optional practice: assign a different title after construction and predict why the parent method reads the current title from the same instance.
after:
`extends` lets one class build on another. `TimedTask` can use the behavior of `Task` and add a duration.

In a child class's constructor, call `super(...)` before using `this`. That runs the parent constructor to set up the instance.

A child class can replace an inherited method. This is called overriding.

`super.describe()` runs the parent's version on the same task. Our version adds the minutes to its text. Calling `this.describe()` here would call our version again and again.

Complete `TimedTask` and keep `Task` unchanged. Accept a title string and a finite number of minutes that is zero or greater.

Save both values. Make `describe()` return the parent's description followed by ` / `, the minutes, and ` min`. The method should read the task's current values.

before.question: If a TimedTask’s title changes to "Walk" before describe(), what does super.describe() read?
choices: The current title "Walk" on that same instance.
The original title captured forever by super.
before.explanation: super selects the parent method, but the method still receives the existing task as this.

after.question: If a TimedTask’s title changes to "Walk" before describe(), what does super.describe() read?
choices: The current title "Walk" on that same instance.
The original title captured forever by super.
after.explanation: super chooses the parent method, but this is still the same task. The method reads its current title.
